Confirmed — there's no `/api/auth/*` route in `worker/src/index.ts`, and `removeCampaign` is the only consumer of the delete action.

**Login**: Purely client-side, no backend call. `AuthService.login()` (`frontend/src/app/services/auth.service.ts`) takes a username and looks for `localStorage["ai_dnd_user_<username.toLowerCase()>"]`. If found, it loads that `UserProfile`; otherwise it creates `{ username, campaigns: [] }` and persists it via `persist()` to both that per-user key and the "current session" key `ai_dnd_user`. `AuthGuard` (`auth.guard.ts`) just checks `AuthService.isLoggedIn()` (profile !== null). There is no password, token, or server-side session — identity is just a free-text name mapped to a `localStorage` blob.

**Campaigns**: Stored entirely in the browser as `CampaignSlot[]` inside that same `UserProfile` JSON in `localStorage` (model in `frontend/src/app/models/game.models.ts`). Each slot (`slotId`, `characterName`, `characterClass`, `characterRace`, `level`, `sessionId`, `characterId`, `lastPlayed`) just references a D1 `characterId`/KV `sessionId` pair — the actual character data lives server-side in the D1 `characters` table (and KV `session:{id}` for context), created via `worker/src/routes/character.ts` (`POST /api/character/create`).

**Deleting a campaign slot**: `LoginComponent.deleteCampaign()` → `AuthService.removeCampaign(slotId)` (`auth.service.ts` lines 54–60) simply filters the slot out of the local `campaigns` array and re-persists the profile to `localStorage`. **No API call is made** — there's no DELETE route for characters or sessions anywhere in `worker/src/routes/*` (the only `DELETE` endpoint is `character.ts`'s `/:id/inventory/:itemId` for dropping inventory items). So the server-side `characters` row in D1 and its KV session data are never removed — they become orphaned, unreachable only because the client no longer has a slot pointing to them.
